Indicate for each of the following statements about the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) whether it is true or false.

A. Ribosomes bound to the ER membrane produce proteins for the cytoplasm.

B. Calcium ions are stored in the ER.

C. The ER has a smooth and a rough part.

D. The ER exchanges vesicles with the Golgi apparatus.

A. Muscle contraction is triggered by the influx of magnesium ions.

B. Myosin has ATP-binding pockets.

C. Actin filaments and myosin filaments are involved in muscle contraction.

D. A myofibril consists of several muscle fibres.

A. The rough endoplasmic reticulum is covered with lysosomes.

C. Chloroplasts are important for the photosynthesis of plants.

B. Being made up of several cells

C. Own genetic material

D. Independent locomotion

B. Catalysis of chemical reactions

C. Transport of molecules

A. Investigating whether two different DNA samples come from the same person.

B. Generating a protein sequence from mRNA.

C. Generating an RNA molecule from a known DNA sequence.

B. Mitochondrion

C. Ribosome

D. Nucleus

Phosphofructokinase (PFK) is an enzyme that regulates ATP production during the breakdown of glucose. If enough ATP is present, ATP inhibits PFK. To do so, ATP binds to PFK outside the active site. This binding changes the 3D structure of the enzyme so that the substrate can no longer bind. When ATP detaches from PFK, the enzyme becomes active again. What type of regulation is this?

A. Inhibition of protein synthesis.

B. Allosteric inhibition.

C. Competitive inhibition.

D. Irreversible inhibition.

Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles of eukaryotic cells. They contain digestive enzymes and have an acidic pH inside. Their task is to break down biopolymers. Assume that all lysosomes in a cell suddenly burst. What would be possible consequences? Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The cell bursts because the osmotic pressure increases.

B. DNA in chloroplasts is degraded.

C. The pH in the cytoplasm decreases.

D. Proteins, lipids and polysaccharides in the cytoplasm are degraded.

Indicate for each of the following processes whether it takes place in the cell nucleus (true) or not (false)?

A. DNA replication

B. Translation of mRNA

C. Transcription of genes

D. Transcription of mitochondrial DNA

B. The cell membrane of plant cells consists of cellulose.

C. Carbohydrates have the general molecular formula $C_nH_{2\ast n}O_n$.

A. Vinegar impedes bacterial cellular respiration.

B. The pH of vinegar prevents many bacteria from growing.

C. Vinegar forms a hypertonic medium.

D. Vinegar impedes the cellular respiration of fungi.

A. The vacuole of plant cells is responsible for photosynthesis.

B. The plant cell contains mitochondria.

C. Plant cells have a cell wall.

D. Both plant and animal cells have chloroplasts.

The Michaelis–Menten model describes the catalysis of enzymatic reactions. It is based on the following concept:

$$\mathrm{E} + \mathrm{S} \underset{k_{off}}{\overset{k_{on}}{\rightleftharpoons}} [\mathrm{ES}] \xrightarrow{k_{cat}} \mathrm{P} + \mathrm{E}$$

From this model, the following function can be described:

$$v_0 = \frac{v_{max} \cdot [S]}{K_m + [S]}$$

$v_0$: initial rate

$v_{max}$: maximum reaction rate

$K_m$: Michaelis constant ([S] at which half the maximum rate is reached.)
